# Erdős-Szemerédi Sunflower Conjecture

The Erdős-Szemerédi sunflower conjecture asserts that, for every integer Image: k>=3, there is a constant Image: c_k<2 such that a family of subsets of Image: [n]={1,...,n} containing no Image: k-member sunflower has at most Image: c_k^n members, for Image: n>=k-1 (Bucić et al. 2026). A sunflower consists of distinct sets whose pairwise intersections are equal.

Bucić et al. (2026) proved the quantitative bound

Image: |F|<=3(2-1/(16k^3))^n 

for every integer Image: n>=1 and Image: k>=3. Together with the elementary strict bound Image: |F|<2^n when Image: n>=k-1, this proves the conjecture. The result concerns families on a fixed ground set. It does not settle the uniform sunflower conjecture, which instead bounds families of fixed-size sets independently of the size of their ground set.

Bucić et al. (2026) report that ChatGPT originated the key vector-sunflower argument. The authors rewrote and checked the proof. They report a Lean verification whose public release was forthcoming.

# Proof of the Erdős-Szemerédi sunflower conjecture

Matija Bucić, Fankang He, Hyunwoo Lee

  * Mathematics

For integers k≥3 and D,n≥1, a k-sunflower-free family in [D]^n has size at most ((2k)^(2/(k−1)) D^(1−1/(k−1)))^n. Here a vector sunflower has entries all equal or pairwise distinct in every coordinate. The authors’ reduction gives the set-family bound 3(2−1/(16k³))^n and resolves the Erdős–Szemerédi conjecture for every k≥3.

## Sources for this record

  * Original claimBucić, He and Lee: sunflower theorem and AI disclosurearxiv.org

## What was already known

The k=3 case followed from the 2016 cap-set breakthrough and earlier vector-to-set reductions. The general k case remained open. GPT supplied Theorem 2; the authors rewrote its slice-rank proof in polynomial-method language and completed the quantitative reduction to set families.

## AI involvement AI-centered

The authors credit ChatGPT 6 Astra Pro with finding the proof of Theorem 2 after a short discussion asking it to generalize Naslund–Sawin’s k=3 argument. Humans posed that direction, rewrote the reasoning and supplied the reduction and applications. The retained AI contribution is the central vector theorem, not sole authorship of every result.

## Importance Major

The central vector bound supplies the missing exponential saving for a longstanding extremal-set problem.

## Limitations

This is the nonuniform Erdős–Szemerédi sunflower conjecture. The uniform Erdős–Rado sunflower conjecture remains open. Human checking is reported by the authors; the promised Lean artifact is not yet available in the reviewed public sources.

# Erdős–Szemerédi sunflower conjecture proved for every k ≥ 3

The key vector bound (Theorem 2) was found by ChatGPT 6 Astra Pro (Bucić, He, Lee)

Importance: historic (5 of 5)

Researched and written by AI agents (Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code). Human editor: Adam Bicz.

The takeaway

A 1970s Erdős–Szemerédi conjecture is claimed proved for every k: families of subsets of [n] with no k-sunflower have size at most c_k^n with c_k < 2. Before this only k = 3 was known, through the 2016 cap-set breakthrough. The authors say ChatGPT 6 Astra Pro found the proof of the central theorem. The paper also says a Lean check exists, but it has not been released yet.

## Key facts

  * Paper: ‘Proof of the Erdős-Szemerédi sunflower conjecture’, Matija Bucić, Fankang He (Faculty of Mathematics, University of Vienna), Hyunwoo Lee (KAIST and IBS ECOPRO), arXiv 2610.26686 [math.CO], submitted 19 Oct 2026
  * Conjecture (abstract): ‘In the 1970s, Erdős and Szemerédi conjectured that for any n ≥ k − 1 ≥ 2, any collection of subsets of [n] not containing a k-sunflower has size at most c_k^n for some c_k < 2.’ The original argument it produced used the slice-rank terminology due to Tao (as used in [45]); we rewrote it in the polynomial method language … The authors have verified all the results in the paper and take full responsibility for the content. The proof has been verified in Lean 4.35; the verification will be made available on the Palomar repository.’ ([45] is Naslund–Sawin)
  * Concurrent work cited in the paper: another team proves that the set-sunflower relation on the Boolean cube has maximal slice rank, and ‘They discuss extensive use of AI, including multi-agent setups’. The authors say that obstruction concerns set sunflowers, while their tester is for vector sunflowers, so it does not apply
  * Consequences listed in the paper: the vector bound extends the Alon–Shpilka–Umans question (connected to fast matrix multiplication) and gives results in arithmetic property testing and on equal subset sums

## What happened

A sunflower is a family of sets whose pairwise intersections are all the same set. Erdős and Szemerédi asked how large a family of subsets of an n-element set can be without containing k sets forming a sunflower, and conjectured an exponential saving over the trivial 2^n. The k = 3 case became a corollary of the 2016 cap-set breakthrough. Bucić, He and Lee had asked ChatGPT 6 Astra Pro to generalize Naslund and Sawin’s k = 3 slice-rank argument for a different problem, the induced Erdős–Sauer problem. The model produced a bound for vector sunflowers that works for all k, and with the authors’ reduction this gives the full conjecture.

The authors rewrote the model’s slice-rank argument in polynomial-method language. They say all results were verified, including in Lean 4.35, but the formal proof had not been posted when the preprint appeared.

## Why it matters

This is one of the best-known problems in extremal set theory. It sits next to the Erdős–Rado sunflower conjecture, which stays open, and is tied to cap sets and the group-theoretic approach to matrix multiplication. The authors credit the model with the proof of the key theorem, not with exposition, which puts it among the strongest AI contributions to combinatorics so far. Until the Lean files are released or experts review it, the claim stays pending.

Only the three-petal case (k = 3) was settled, in 2016, through the breakthrough on the cap set problem and a reduction due to Alon, Shpilka and Umans.

## The bound

Matija Bucić and Fankang He (University of Vienna) and Hyunwoo Lee (KAIST and the Institute for Basic Science, South Korea) prove the conjecture for every k ≥ 3. Their main theorem: a collection with no k-petal sunflower has at most

3 · (2 − 1/(16k³))ⁿ

members. The base sits just below 2, but it is a fixed number below 2, and that is exactly what Erdős and Szemerédi asked for. A construction from 1997 shows that, for large k, the truth cannot be much lower.

## From sets to vectors

The proof goes through a version of the problem with vectors. Split the numbers into n blocks of D elements and choose one element per block: each choice is a vector. Several vectors form a sunflower when, in every position, their entries are either all equal or all different.

The authors then build a “sunflower tester”: a function that, on a sunflower-free collection, is non-zero only when all its inputs are the same vector. The new ingredient is to write this function, step by step, with interpolation polynomials of low degree. Counting those polynomials bounds the size of the collection (their Theorem 2). A probabilistic argument, random blocks averaged over all set sizes, carries the bound back to ordinary sets.

## Found by a machine, checked by another

The paper’s statement on AI is unusually direct. The proof of Theorem 2 was found by ChatGPT 6 Astra Pro, after a short discussion that began by asking it to generalise the known three-petal argument. The authors needed that step for another goal: an induced version of a graph problem posed by Szemerédi, which they announce for a later note.

The model wrote its proof in the language of “slice rank”. The authors rewrote it in the language of the polynomial method, which they find easier for readers. They state that they verified every result and take full responsibility, and that the proof has been verified in Lean 4.35, a proof-checking software, with the verification to be posted on the Palomar repository.

## What it does not settle

The authors did not try to optimise the base. For three petals, it does not beat the 2017 bound of Naslund and Sawin, about 1.89. And the stronger sister problem, the Erdős–Rado sunflower conjecture, remains open: their bounds still depend heavily on the block size D, which is exactly what that problem forbids.

## #1 Proof of the Erdős-Szemerédi sunflower conjecture [PDF^{}] [Copy] [Kimi^{}] [REL]

Authors: Matija Bucić, Fankang He, Hyunwoo Lee

In the 1970s, Erdős and Szemerédi conjectured that for any $n \ge k-1\ge 2$, any collection of subsets of $[n]$ not containing a $k$-sunflower has size at most $c_k^n$ for some $c_k<2$. In the $k=3$ case, this follows from the work of Croot, Lev, and Pach and Ellenberg and Gijswijt on the cap-set problem, through a reduction due to Alon, Shpilka, and Umans. We prove the conjecture for every $k \ge 3$.

Let $f(k,s)$ denote the minimum integer $m$ such that any family $\mathcal{F}$ consisting of $k$-sized sets of cardinality at least $m$ always contain a sunflower of size $s$. The Erdős-Rado Sunflower Conjecture states that for every $s >2$, there is an constant $C=C(s)$ such that $f(k,s) \leq C^k$. In this paper, we prove the conjecture.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Derandomized Sunflowers and Radical Lower Bounds

TR26-220 Authors: Bruno Pasqualotto Cavalar, Théo Fabris, Partha Mukhopadhyay, Srikanth Srinivasan, Amir Yehudayoff
Publication: 28th September 2026 18:10
Downloads: 563

Keywords: 

Derandomization of Robust Sunflower lemmas, Monotone Arithmetic Circuits, monotone Boolean circuits, Nisan-Wigderson designs, the method of moments

Abstract:

Robust Sunflower lemmas imply that any large enough monotone DNF of width $w$ contains a sunflower, i.e., a DNF equivalent to the conjunction of a common core with a DNF that is heavily biased towards $1$. While these lemmas are typically proved in the context of the uniform distribution or i.i.d. distributions, they also hold for $O(w^2)$-wise independent distributions by Bazzi's theorem (Bazzi (SICOMP 2009); Tal (CCC 2017)), which states that width-$w$ DNFs cannot distinguish between such distributions and the uniform distribution.
